Effective diplomacy, using a network of allies, and an inclusive approach to conquered peoples also helped. This approach strengthened and broadened Roman power and logistical support. Furthermore, Rome's allies supplied, equipped, and paid for additional soldiers. They also provided vital materials such as grain and ships. In addition to all this, Rome was almost always at war or prepared for it. Romans firmly believed in defending and imposing what they considered their cultural superiority.

All these __factors/objects/functions/elements__ build confidence. Having said all this, it has to be assumed that if someone becomes a leader, at some point they understood the difference between right and wrong. It is up to them to __abide/remain/stand/conform__ by a moral code and up to us to ensure that the moment we suspect they do not, we fire them or vote them out.

items.title: #701 Arbitration

items.fullText: Arbitration is a method of conflict resolution which, with more or less formalized mechanisms, occurs in many political and legal spheres. There are two main characteristics to arbitration. The first is that it is a voluntary process under which two parties in conflict agree between themselves to be bound by the judgment of a third party which has no other authority over them; the judgment, however, is not legally binding. The second is that there is usually no clear body of laws or set of rules that must apply; the arbitrator is free, subject to any prior agreement with the conflicting parties, to decide on whatever basis of justice is deemed suitable .
items.beginnerText:
Arbitration helps solve arguments. It happens in law and politics. There are two main things about it.
First, it is voluntary. Two groups in a fight both agree to listen to a third group. This third group does not have power over them. But both groups agree to follow their decision. However, the decision is not legally required.
Second, there are usually no clear laws. The person who helps decide (the arbitrator) can choose what is fair. They can do this if both groups agree.

First, it is a voluntary process. Two groups in a conflict agree to accept the decision of a third party. This third party does not have authority over them. However, the decision is not legally binding.
Second, there are usually no clear laws that must be followed. The arbitrator can decide based on what seems fair, if the conflicting groups agree.

items.title: #704 DNA Barcoding
items.answerText: DNA barcoding was invented by Paul Hebert of the University of Guelph, in Ontario, Canada, in 2003. His idea was to __generate/create/get/make__ a unique identification tag for each species based on a short __stretch/line/period/cut__ of DNA. Separating species would then be a simple task of sequencing this tiny bit of DNA. Dr Hebert proposed part of a gene called cytochrome c oxidase I (COI) as suitable to the task. All animals have it. It seems to vary enough, but not too much, to act as a reliable marker. And it is easily __extracted/bought/made/get__ ,because it is one of a handful of genes found outside the cell nucleus, in structures called mitochondria. Barcoding has taken off rapidly since Dr Hebert invented it. When the idea was proposed, it was expected to be a __boon/gift/present/curse__ to taxonomists trying to name the world's millions of species. It has, however, proved to have a far wider range of uses than the merely academic-- most promisingly in the __realm/period/world/range__ of public health. items.fullText: Our analysis of the genetic structure of northern spotted owls across most of the range of the subspecies allowed us to test for genetic discontinuities and identify landscape features that influence the subspecies' genetic structure. Although no distinct genetic breaks were found in northern spotted owls, several landscape features were important in structuring genetic variation. Dry, low elevation valleys and the high elevation Cascade and Olympic Mountains restricted gene flow, while the lower Oregon Coast Range facilitated gene flow, acting as a 'genetic corridor.' The Columbia River did not act as a barrier, suggesting owls readily fly over this large river. We did not find big changes in their genes. But some parts of the land changed their genes. Dry valleys and high mountains stopped genes from mixing. They are connected by cartilage, such as in the spine. Each vertebra in the spine moves relative to the ones above and below, and these movements together provide the spine's flexibility. Freely movable, or synovial, joints allow movement in multiple directions. The body's main joints, including those at the hip, shoulders, elbows, knees, wrists, and ankles, are freely movable. They contain synovial fluid, which acts as a lubricant to facilitate easy joint movement. Three types of freely movable joints are crucial for voluntary movement: Hinge joints, such as those in the knees and elbows, allow movement in one direction. Pivot joints, like the one allowing the head to move from side to side, enable rotating or twisting motion. Ball-and-socket joints, found in the hips and shoulders, offer the greatest freedom of movement. In this type of joint, the rounded end of a long bone fits into the hollow of another bone.

items.beginnerText: Populations can change in three ways. These are fertility, mortality, and migration. Fertility is about the number of children women have. This is different from fecundity (a woman's ability to have children). Mortality is the study of what causes death in a group of people. It also looks at what happens because of death. Demographers often study mortality using the Life Table. The Life Table is a way to get information about death. It tells us how long people are expected to live. Migration is when people move from one place to another. They cross a political border to get there. Migration experts only count moves that are permanent. items.intermediateText: Populations can change through three processes: fertility, mortality, and migration. Fertility refers to the number of children women have, differing from fecundity (a woman's potential to have children). Mortality is the study of the causes, effects, and measurement of factors influencing death in a population. While demographers studying migration often use census data on place of residence, indirect data sources such as tax forms and labor force surveys are also important. Demography is now widely taught in many universities worldwide, attracting students with backgrounds in social sciences, statistics, or health studies.

items.title: #725 Sigmund Freud

Nor is there any doubt that at all times there was both fervent enthusiasm over and bitter hostility to his ideas and influence. Strikingly, Freud emerged as a twentieth-century icon without the endorsement and support of an institution or a profession (in contrast to Einstein, Curie and Russell). items.beginnerText: Sigmund Freud became very important in twentieth-century culture. This is clear. People were both very excited about and very against his ideas. But how Freud became so important, like Karl Marx, Albert Einstein, Marie Curie, and Bertrand Russell, is not clear. This happened even though some people did not like him. Freud became a big icon in the twentieth-century. He did not have the support of a big group or job, unlike Einstein, Curie, and Russell. How did he become so famous? This book will show how this happened in one place: Cambridge. Cambridge was and is a university town in England with a small population.
items.intermediateText: It is certain that Sigmund Freud became a major intellectual figure in twentieth-century culture. It is also clear that his ideas were met with both great enthusiasm and strong opposition. However, it is not fully understood how Freud, despite this hostility, became a master of intellectual life, similar to Karl Marx, Albert Einstein, Marie Curie, and Bertrand Russell in the 1920s. Notably, Freud became a twentieth-century icon without the backing of an institution or profession, unlike Einstein, Curie, and Russell. Where can we find the details of how this new figure gained immense cultural authority? One of the main goals of this book is to explain how this occurred in one specific place: Cambridge. Cambridge was, and still is, a university town in the English Fens with a relatively small and changing population.

items.title: #726 High-protein Diet
items.answerText: In our studies, those people on a high-protein diet lost the same amount of weight as those on a higher-carbohydrate diet, since the two diets __offered/suffered/done/created__ an equal amount of kilojoules and the same amount of fat. When the __participants/researchers/audience/scientists__ in other studies were allowed to eat until they were no longer hungry, those on the higher protein diet lost more weight than those on the higher carbohydrate diet, even after more than a year. The reduction in hunger and the beneficial effect on muscle provided by the higher-protein diet is mostly related to its protein content, while the reduced triglyceride levels and enhanced fat-loss seem to be related to its lower amounts of carbohydrate. The diet is healthy because its protein comes from lean red meat, fish, chicken and low-fat dairy products, all of which __provide/release/consisting/provides__ good nutrition. A high-protein diet in which the protein comes from protein powders and supplements is unlikely to be healthy, unless the supplements are __fortified/supplied/interacted/teemed__ with vitamins and minerals.

But, body composition (how much fat and muscle you have) got better for those on the high-protein diet. In other studies, people could eat until full. Those on the high-protein diet lost more weight than those on the high-carbohydrate diet, even after a year. The high-protein diet made people less hungry and helped their muscles. This is because of the protein in the diet. Also, it lowered triglyceride levels and helped with fat loss because it had less carbohydrate. A high-protein diet that gets its protein from protein powders and supplements is unlikely to be healthy, unless the supplements have added vitamins and minerals.

items.title: #728 Computer
items.answerText: The purpose of this paper is to consider the claim, often made, that computer simulation exercises provide an excellent source of speaking practice. In so doing I shall first consider the properties of computer simulations from a theoretical __point of view/shape or form/state of mind/aspect__ , then describe the experience of __using/used/being used/having been used__ a particular simulation with a general EFL class. On the basis of this experience, and of some very straightforward pedagogical considerations, I shall argue that the claim is justified, __subject/reject/expect/inject__ to a very important caveat: computer simulations can form the basis of excellent speaking exercises, provided you do not expect the computer to do all the work. Put in another way, many computer simulations only __attain/obtain/retain/remain__ their full potential as language exercises if they are __integrated/separated/included/participated__ into a larger, planned, teacher-managed activity.
items.fullText: The purpose of this paper is to consider the claim, often made, that computer simulation exercises provide an excellent source of speaking practice. In so doing I shall first consider the properties of computer simulations from a theoretical point of view , then describe the experience of using a particular simulation with a general EFL class. On the basis of this experience, and of some very straightforward pedagogical considerations, I shall argue that the claim is justified, subject to a very important caveat: computer simulations can form the basis of excellent speaking exercises, provided you do not expect the computer to do all the work. items.beginnerText: This paper looks at the idea that computer games are good for speaking practice. First, I will talk about what computer games are like in theory. Then, I will talk about using one game with an English class. Based on this, I will say that the idea is right. But there is one important thing to remember: computer games can be good for speaking, if you don't think the computer will do everything. In other words, computer games are only really good for learning languages if they are part of a bigger activity that the teacher plans and controls.
items.intermediateText: This paper aims to examine the common claim that computer simulation exercises offer a great way to practice speaking. To do this, I will first look at the characteristics of computer simulations from a theoretical perspective. Then, I will describe my experience of using a specific simulation with a general EFL (English as a Foreign Language) class. Based on this experience, and some simple teaching ideas, I will argue that the claim is correct, but with one important condition. Computer simulations can be excellent for speaking exercises if you don't expect the computer to do all the work. In other words, many computer simulations only reach their full potential as language exercises when they are included in a larger, planned, teacher-led activity.

items.title: #729 Bad Title

They go to __infinite/stagnant/faint/disastrous__ pains to make the story itself fresh and individual, and then cap it with a __commonplace/perplexing/invisible/distinctive__ phrase that is worse than no title at all. A good title is apt, specific, attractive, new, and short. A title is apt if it is an outgrowth of the plot — a text, as I have said. Novices are peculiarly liable to this fault, usually through allowing themselves to be too easily satisfied. They go to infinite pains to make the story itself fresh and individual, and then cap it with a commonplace phrase that is worse than no title at all. A good title is apt, specific, attractive, new, and short. A title is apt if it is an outgrowth of the plot — a text, as I have said. items.beginnerText: A good story can fail if the title is bad. New writers often make this mistake because they are too happy with their titles. They work hard to make the story good, but then give it a boring title. This is worse than having no title. A good title is fitting, clear, interesting, new, and short. A good title comes from the story itself. It shows what the story is about and gives a hint of what will happen. But it should not give away the ending.
items.intermediateText: A good story can be ruined by a bad title chosen by the author, leading it towards failure. New writers often make this mistake because they are too easily satisfied with their titles. They put a lot of effort into making the story original, but then ruin it with a common title that is worse than having no title at all. A good title should be fitting, specific, attractive, new, and short. A title is fitting if it comes from the plot of the story. It clearly represents that story and suggests what will happen, but it should only be a suggestion, so it does not reveal the ending too soon.

The APS Division of Psychological Research, Education and Training, in consultation with teacher and curriculum representatives from every State and Territory in Australia, develops a proposed framework for senior secondary school studies in psychological science. This framework is modeled on the current senior science curricula that were developed and published by the Australian Curriculum, Assessment and Reporting Authority. The APS hopes that this framework will facilitate a dialogue between educators and their local curriculum authority, with the aim of working towards a more consistent approach to the teaching of psychological science at secondary school level and optimizing the preparation for students going on to undergraduate psychology studies at university, as well as the effective use of psychological principles in everyday life.

They are making a plan for high school studies in psychological science. This plan is like the current science plans made by the Australian Curriculum, Assessment and Reporting Authority. This framework is based on current senior science curricula created by the Australian Curriculum, Assessment and Reporting Authority. The APS hopes this framework will encourage discussion between educators and their local curriculum authorities. The goal is to create a more consistent way of teaching psychological science in secondary schools. This should also improve how well students are prepared for undergraduate psychology studies at university, and promote the effective use of psychological principles in everyday life.

items.title: #731 Mass-communications

This would be to think of the __process/works/practice/production__ as a ' complex structure in dominance' , sustained through the articulation of connected practices, each of which, however, retains its distinctiveness and has its own __specific/general/real/common__ modality, its own forms and conditions of existence.
items.fullText: Traditionally, mass-communications research has conceptualized the process of communication in terms of a circulation circuit or loop. This model has been criticized for its linearity -- sender/message/receiver -- for its concentration on the level of message exchange and for the absence of a structured conception of the different moments as a complex structure of relations. But it is possible (and is useful ) to think of this process in terms of a structure produced and sustained through the articulation of linked and distinctive moments production, circulation, distribution/consumption, reproduction. This would be to think of the process as a ' complex structure in dominance' , sustained through the articulation of connected practices, each of which, however, retains its distinctiveness and has its own specific modality, its own forms and conditions of existence.
items.beginnerText: In the past, research about mass communication saw communication as a circle or loop. People did not like this idea because it was too simple (sender/message/receiver). It focused too much on the message. It did not see the different parts as connected. But we can think of communication as a structure. This structure is made and kept going by connecting different parts. These parts are production, circulation, distribution/consumption, and reproduction. We can think of communication as a 'complex structure in dominance'. It is kept going by connected actions. Each action is different and has its own way of being.
items.intermediateText: Traditionally, research in mass communication has viewed communication as a circulation circuit or loop. This model has been criticized because it is too linear, with a simple sender/message/receiver approach. It focuses too much on the message exchange and lacks a structured view of the different parts as a complex system of relations. However, it is possible and useful to consider this process as a structure created and maintained through the connection of different parts: production, circulation, distribution/consumption, and reproduction. This means seeing the process as a 'complex structure in dominance', supported by connected practices. Each practice keeps its own unique features and has its own specific way of functioning, with its own conditions and forms.

items.title: #732 EE&AVG
items.answerText: There has been increased research interest in the use of active video games (in which players physically interact with images onscreen) as a means to __promote/examine/obstruct/inspect__ physical activity in children. The aim of this review was to assess active video games as a means of increasing energy expenditure and physical activity behavior in children. Studies were obtained from computerized searches of multiple electronic bibliographic databases. The last search was conducted in December 2008. Eleven studies focused on the quantification of the energy cost associated with playing active video games, and eight studies focused on the utility of active video games as an __intervention/inversion/infusion/aversion__ to increase physical activity in children. Compared with traditional non-active video games, active video games __elicited/consumed/reduced/spread__ greater energy expenditure, which was similar in intensity to mild to moderate intensity physical activity. The intervention studies indicate that active video games may have the potential to increase free-living physical activity and improve body __composition/element/tissue/nutrition__ in children; however, methodological limitations prevent __definitive/optimal/positive/optimistic__ conclusions. Future research should focus on larger, methodologically sound intervention trials to provide definitive answers as to whether this technology is effective in __promoting/obstructing/reviewing/assessing__ long-term physical activity in children.

The aim of this review was to assess active video games as a means of increasing energy expenditure and physical activity behavior in children. Studies were obtained from computerized searches of multiple electronic bibliographic databases. The last search was conducted in December 2008. Compared with traditional non-active video games, active video games elicited greater energy expenditure, which was similar in intensity to mild to moderate intensity physical activity. The intervention studies indicate that active video games may have the potential to increase free-living physical activity and improve body composition in children; however, methodological limitations prevent definitive conclusions. Future research should focus on larger, methodologically sound intervention trials to provide definitive answers as to whether this technology is effective in promoting long-term physical activity in children.
items.beginnerText: More researchers are interested in active video games. In these games, players move their bodies to play. The games may help children be more active. This review looked at active video games. It checked if they help children use more energy and be more active. Researchers found studies by searching computer databases. The last search was in December 2008. Eleven studies looked at how much energy kids use when playing active video games. Eight studies looked at if these games help kids be more active. Active video games made kids use more energy than normal video games. The energy used was like doing light exercise. The studies showed active video games might help kids be more active and have healthier bodies. But, the studies had problems. So, we cannot be sure. More research is needed to know if these games can help children be active for a long time.
items.intermediateText: There is growing research interest in using active video games to encourage physical activity in children. Active video games require players to physically interact with what they see on the screen. This review aimed to assess if active video games can increase energy use and physical activity in children. Studies were found by searching electronic databases. The last search was done in December 2008. Eleven studies looked at how much energy is used when playing active video games. Eight studies examined if active video games could help children become more physically active. Compared to regular video games, active video games caused greater energy use, similar to mild to moderate exercise. The studies suggest that active video games might increase regular physical activity and improve body composition in children. However, because of some issues with how the studies were done, we cannot draw firm conclusions. Future research should involve larger, well-designed studies to determine if this technology effectively promotes long-term physical activity in children.

items.title: #733 Transportation System

items.fullText: A sustainable transportation system is one in which people's needs and desires for access to jobs, commerce, recreation, culture and home are accommodated using a minimum of resources. Applying principles of sustainability to transportation will reduce pollution generated by gasoline-powered engines, noise, traffic congestion, land devaluation, urban sprawl, economic segregation, and injury to drivers, pedestrians and cyclists. In addition, the costs of commuting, shipping, housing and goods will be reduced . Ultimately in a sustainable San Francisco, almost all trips to and within the City will be on public transit, foot or bicycle-as will a good part of trips to the larger Bay Region. Walking through streets designed for pedestrians and bicycles will be more pleasant than walking through those designed for the automobile. Street-front retail and commercial establishments will prosper from the large volume of foot traffic drawn to an environment enhanced by trees, appropriately designed 'street furniture' ( street lights, bicycle racks, benches, and the like) and other people. items.beginnerText: A sustainable transport system uses few resources to meet people's needs. These needs are for jobs, shopping, fun, culture, and home. Using sustainable transport can lower pollution from cars. It can also lower noise, traffic, and damage to land. It can help stop urban sprawl and separation of people by money. It can also prevent injuries to drivers, walkers, and cyclists. Also, the costs of travel, shipping, homes, and goods will be less. In a sustainable San Francisco, almost all trips in the city will be by bus, walking, or bike. Many trips to the Bay Region will be too. Walking on streets for walkers and bikes will be nicer than walking on streets for cars. Shops will do well because many people will walk by. Trees and street furniture (like lights and benches) will make it a nice place to walk. Rent and property costs will be lower because parking lots will not be needed.
items.intermediateText: A sustainable transportation system meets people's needs and desires for jobs, shopping, recreation, culture, and housing while using few resources. Using sustainability in transportation will reduce pollution from gasoline engines, noise, traffic jams, falling land values, urban sprawl, economic segregation, and injuries to drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists. Also, the costs of commuting, shipping, housing, and goods will decrease. In a sustainable San Francisco, almost all trips within the city will be on public transport, by foot, or by bicycle. Many trips to the larger Bay Region will be as well. Walking on streets designed for pedestrians and bicycles will be more enjoyable than walking on streets designed for cars. Shops will benefit from the large number of pedestrians attracted to an area improved by trees, well-designed 'street furniture' (such as street lights and bicycle racks), and other people. Rent and property costs will be lower because land for off-street parking will be less necessary.

items.title: #734 Guilt and Responsibility
items.answerText: The narrative of law and order is located fundamentally at the level of individual guilt and responsibility. items.title: #756 Effective Management
items.answerText: Effective management involves four primary functions and related skill sets: planning, organizing, leading, and controlling. Although there’s a logical sequence to the functions, in practice the four functions are often performed in a dynamic manner. For example, a manager would need to develop or __reference/occurrence/preference/conference__ a departmental or organizational plan prior to executing on it just as you would reference a map prior to __embarking/clicking/relying/bidding__ on a road trip. The proverb ‘if you fail to prepare you are preparing to fail’ __underscores/underfeeds/undercounts/understates__ the importance of this function. However, just as when road or airport closures or other factors might cause you to change your original route, unanticipated internal or external factors might cause a manager to revisit and revise the original plan, requiring a change in the other functions and __associated/enunciated/glaciated/appreciated__ tasks. Thus, achieving organizational goals – arriving at your intended destination – requires ongoing management of the process and an understanding of the interrelationship of the four functions.

items.title: #757 Organizing
items.answerText: Once plans are made, decisions must be made about how to best __implement/couplement/supplement/complement__ the plans. The organizing function involves deciding how the organization will be structured (by departments, matrix teams, job responsibilities, etc.). Organizing involves assigning authority and responsibility to various departments, __allocating/duplicating/certificating/devastating__ resources across the organization, and defining how the activities of groups and individuals will be coordinated. In the case of ThyssenKrupp AG, the management had to __determine/examine/ermine/undermine__ how to support two very different sets of activities in order to achieve its long-term goal. Management needed to continue steel production activities to provide continuity of funds as the emphasis gradually shifted to elevator production. It also had to develop new skills and resources to build the company’s elevator capabilities. A new organizational structure was needed that could support both business activities as one was downsized and the other built up.

A new organizational structure was necessary to support both business activities as one was downsized and the other expanded.

items.title: #758 Environmental Factors
items.answerText: Weather, climate change, air quality, and natural disasters are all environmental factors. Some industries are __especially/necessarily/remotely/spatially__ at risk from changes in the natural environment, including manufacturing, agriculture, tourism and travel, and sports and entertainment. Many pollution regulations limiting water and air pollution have been passed that affect the __operation/deterioration/decoration/transaction__ of businesses. Today, the impact of climate control is being debated in Congress, and organizations in many industries are __concerned/discerning/concerning/discerned__ how this latest environmental threat will affect their operations. Recently, Shell Oil spent more than $7 billion exploring parts of the Arctic Circle for oil – a __venture/vulture/motion/motive__ that was not possible before global warming increased drilling access in the area. They have since cancelled this initiative due to a lack of results, as well as strong international __protests/detests/digests/contests__ that it may cause further damage to an environmentally sensitive location.

items.title: #759 One-dimensional Characters
items.answerText: Characters that lack internal conflict or multiple facets to their personality are often __dubbed/enacted/functioned/acted__ as flat or one-dimensional characters. This is often seen as a bad thing in a story, especially for first-time writers, when all of the characters are one-dimensional. However, if there are one or two characters that are simplistic in nature for a reason, it may not be perceived as a negative __trait/mop/bait/audience__ .As long as an author uses one-dimensional characters correctly, and with deliberate intention, there is nothing wrong with it. Often, a narrative is most successful with a __combination/rejuvenation/determination/inclination__ of flat and rounded characters. With that said, it's important to have strong character development overall to create rounded characters that have some depth to them. This helps characters __imitate/intimidate/humiliate/instate__ being a real human being. Being able to relate to characters in this way, as a reader, makes them far more interesting and realistic.

items.title: #760 Push-pull Factors
items.answerText: In geographical terms, the push-pull factors are those that drive people away from a place and __draw/withdraw/tantalize/appeal__ people to a new location. A combination of push-pull factors helps determine migration or immigration of particular populations from one land to another. Push factors are often forceful, __demanding/resigning/contending/commending__ that a certain person or group of people leave one country for another, or at least giving that person or people strong reasons to want to move — either because of a threat of violence or the loss of financial security. Pull factors, on the other hand, are often the positive aspects of a different country that encourage people to immigrate in order to seek a better life. While it may seem that push and pull factors are diametrically __opposed/reviewed/attracted/struggled__ , they both come into play when a population or person is considering migrating to a new location.

Push-pull factors help decide if people move from one country to another. Push factors make people want to leave. This could be because of violence or losing money. Pull factors are good things about a new country. These things make people want to move there for a better life. Push and pull factors seem very different. But both are important when people think about moving.

These reasons can include threats of violence or the loss of financial security. Pull factors are the positive things about a different country. These encourage people to move there to find a better life. Although push and pull factors seem opposite, both are important when someone is thinking about moving to a new place.

items.title: #761 Cultural Diffusion
items.answerText: Cultural diffusion is the term used to describe the __spread/fulmination/accommodation/prevention__ of cultural ideas from the core culture regions and the culture hearth. There are three methods of cultural diffusion. The first is called direct diffusion and occurs when two distinct cultures are very close together. Over time, direct contact between the two leads to an __intermingling/interdiction/intermittence/introvert__ of the cultures. Historically this occurred through trade, intermarriage, and sometimes warfare because members of the various cultures interacted with each other for long periods. Forced diffusion or expansion diffusion is the second method of cultural diffusion and takes place when one culture defeats another and forces its beliefs and customs onto the __conquered/engaged/respected/slaughtered__ people. An example of this would be when the Spanish took over lands in the Americas and later forced the original inhabitants to __convert/reply/add/require__ to Roman Catholicism in the 16th and 17th Centuries. The final form of cultural diffusion is indirect diffusion. This type of diffusion happens when cultural ideas are spread through a middleman or even another culture.
items.fullText: Cultural diffusion is the term used to describe the spread of cultural ideas from the core culture regions and the culture hearth. There are three methods of cultural diffusion. The first is called direct diffusion and occurs when two distinct cultures are very close together. Over time, direct contact between the two leads to an intermingling of the cultures. Historically this occurred through trade, intermarriage, and sometimes warfare because members of the various cultures interacted with each other for long periods. Forced diffusion or expansion diffusion is the second method of cultural diffusion and takes place when one culture defeats another and forces its beliefs and customs onto the conquered people. An example of this would be when the Spanish took over lands in the Americas and later forced the original inhabitants to convert to Roman Catholicism in the 16th and 17th Centuries. The final form of cultural diffusion is indirect diffusion. This type of diffusion happens when cultural ideas are spread through a middleman or even another culture.
items.beginnerText: Cultural diffusion is when cultural ideas spread from one place to another. There are three ways this happens. The first way is direct diffusion. This happens when two different cultures are near each other. Over time, the two cultures mix together. In the past, this happened through trade, marriage, or war. People from different cultures spent a lot of time together. The second way is forced diffusion. This is when one culture wins against another. The winning culture makes the losing culture accept its beliefs. For example, the Spanish took land in the Americas. Then, they made the people there become Roman Catholic in the 16th and 17th Centuries. The last way is indirect diffusion. This is when ideas spread through another person or culture.
items.intermediateText: Cultural diffusion is the term for how cultural ideas spread from central regions. There are three types of cultural diffusion. The first is direct diffusion, which occurs when two cultures are close. When cultures have direct contact, they begin to mix. Historically, this happened through trade, marriage, and sometimes war, as people from different cultures interacted. Forced diffusion is the second type. It happens when one culture conquers another and makes the conquered people accept its beliefs and customs. For example, when the Spanish took over land in the Americas, they forced the people living there to become Roman Catholic in the 16th and 17th Centuries. The final type of cultural diffusion is indirect diffusion. This happens when cultural ideas spread through a middleman or another culture.

items.title: #762 Ecotourism
items.answerText: Ecotourism is broadly defined as low impact travel to endangered and often undisturbed locations. It is different from traditional tourism because it allows the traveler to become educated about the areas — both in terms of the physical __landscape/security/symptom/plant__ and cultural characteristics, and often provides funds for conservation and benefits the economic development of places that are frequently impoverished. Ecotourism and other forms of __sustainable/acquired/obtainable/preventable__ travel have their origins with the environmental movement of the 1970s. Ecotourism itself did not become __prevalent/opulent/ambivalent/equivalent__ as a travel concept until the late 1980s. During that time, increasing environmental awareness and a desire to travel to natural locations as opposed to built up tourist locations made ecotourism desirable. Since then, several different organizations __specializing/trivializing/conceptualizing/orientalizing__ in ecotourism have developed and many different people have become experts on it.

items.title: #763 Evolution of Human Beings
items.answerText: Dr. Philip Lieberman of Brown University explained on NPR's "The Human Edge" that after humans __diverged/converged/urged/verged__ from an early-ape ancestor more than 100,000 years ago, the shape of the mouth and vocal tract changed, with the tongue and larynx, or voice box, moving further down the tract. The tongue became more __flexible/irresistible/ineligible/convertible__ and independent and was able to be controlled more precisely. The tongue is attached to the hyoid bone, which is not attached to any other bones in the body. Meanwhile, the human neck grew longer to accommodate the tongue and larynx, and the human mouth grew smaller. The larynx is lower in the throats of humans than it is in chimpanzees, which, along with the increased flexibility of the mouth, tongue, and lips, is what enables humans to speak as well as to change __pitch/ditch/impacts/state__ and sing. The ability to speak and develop language was an enormous advantage for humans. The disadvantage of this __evolutionary/imaginary/preliminary/visionary__ development is that this flexibility comes with an increased risk of food going down the wrong tract and causing choking.

items.title: #764 Air Pollution and Risk
items.answerText: Studies have found that __exposure/enclosure/foreclosure/composure__ to air pollution is linked to a greater risk of depression and suicide. While the effects on the body from breathing dirty air are well-established, an emerging body of research has suggested pollution may also affect mental health. Isobel Braithwaite at University College London and her colleagues looked in __detail/favor/charge/support__ at 25 studies published up to late 2017, for a meta-analysis on the links between the two. They found that someone living for at least six months in an area with twice the World Health Organization’s recommended limit for fine particulate matter, PM2.5, would have roughly a 10 percent increased risk of developing depression as a person living in an area that met the limit. The WHO’s guideline is that PM2.5s shouldn’t __exceed/proceed/succeed/impede__ 10 micrograms per cubic metre of air (μg/m3) on average over a year. This is the average level in the UK. In London the average figure is higher at 13.3μg/m3, and in Delhi it is around 133μg/m3.

items.title: #765 Pollution and Health
items.answerText: A study published today __adds/decides/compares/expects__ to evidence that air pollution may be linked to mental health conditions. But it’s not clear yet how – and if – pollution may be affecting our brains. Analyzing data from 151 million people in the US and 1.4 million people in Denmark, researchers have found that there is a strong __correlation/mortification/gesticulation/citation__ between poor air quality and higher rates of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, personality disorders and major depression. This suggests there is a link, but not necessarily that pollution is causing these conditions. When the team looked at health insurance claims in the US, they found that the strongest __predictor/detector/inspector/collector__ of being diagnosed with bipolar disorder – after ethnicity – was air quality. Previous studies have __unearthed/unsolved/untitled/unfilled__ a correlation in the UK between polluted areas and teenagers reporting psychotic experiences and local air pollution and psychiatric disorders in Swedish children.
items.fullText: A study published today adds to evidence that air pollution may be linked to mental health conditions. But it’s not clear yet how – and if – pollution may be affecting our brains. Analyzing data from 151 million people in the US and 1.4 million people in Denmark, researchers have found that there is a strong correlation between poor air quality and higher rates of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, personality disorders and major depression. This suggests there is a link, but not necessarily that pollution is causing these conditions. When the team looked at health insurance claims in the US, they found that the strongest predictor of being diagnosed with bipolar disorder – after ethnicity – was air quality. Previous studies have unearthed a correlation in the UK between polluted areas and teenagers reporting psychotic experiences and local air pollution and psychiatric disorders in Swedish children.
items.beginnerText: A new study shows that air pollution might be linked to mental health problems. But we don't know how pollution affects our brains. Scientists looked at information from 151 million people in the US and 1.4 million people in Denmark. They found a strong link between bad air and more cases of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, personality disorders, and major depression. This means there might be a connection. But it does not prove that pollution causes these problems. The study also looked at health insurance records in the US. They found that air quality was the biggest sign of bipolar disorder, after ethnicity. Other studies showed a link in the UK between polluted areas and teenagers with psychotic experiences. They also found a link between air pollution and mental problems in Swedish children.
items.intermediateText: A recently published study adds to the evidence suggesting a link between air pollution and mental health conditions. However, the specific ways in which pollution might affect our brains remain unclear. Researchers analyzed data from 151 million people in the US and 1.4 million people in Denmark. They found a strong correlation between poor air quality and higher rates of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, personality disorders, and major depression. This suggests a potential link, although it doesn't definitively prove that pollution causes these conditions. Analyzing health insurance claims in the US, the researchers discovered that air quality was the strongest predictor of a bipolar disorder diagnosis, second only to ethnicity. Furthermore, previous studies in the UK have revealed a correlation between polluted areas and teenagers reporting psychotic experiences, as well as between local air pollution and psychiatric disorders in Swedish children.

items.title: #766 High Levels of Anxiety

Someone who is blind but perceives flashes of light and color from Charles Bonnet syndrome may include these experiences in their dreams.

England in 1601 enacted the Poor Law, which recognized the state's responsibility to the aged, although programs were carried out by local church parishes. An amendment to this law in 1834 instituted workhouses for the poor and aged, and in 1925 England introduced social insurance for the aged regulated by statistical evaluations. In 1940 programs for the aged came under England's welfare state system. In the 1880s Otto von Bismarck in Germany introduced old-age pensions whose model was followed by most other western European countries. The United States was among the last to establish such programs. It wasn't until the Social Security Act of 1935, designed to ease the difficulties of the Great Depression, that the elderly received old-age pensions. While these government programs ease some of the burdens of aging, they generally do not provide older individuals with an income comparable to that of younger individuals.

The numerous sudden changes that __evoke/prioritize/possess/ventilate__ rapid and short-term responses via the nervous and hormonal systems are not examples of acclimatization. An individual organism can regulate its internal processes rapidly to sustain itself within the usual range of environmental changes that it __encounters/counters/reimburses/succumbs__ hourly or daily. But this rapid regulation, or homeostasis, is limited in its operation to a small range of environmental variations. Homeostatic regulation usually cannot meet effectively large environmental changes such as those that would allow a plant or animal living in the warmth of summer to __function/conjunction/cite/construct__ in the cold of winter. As summer wanes, organisms change their substance and their habits in seeming anticipation of the coming winter. This gradual adjustment to conditions is acclimatization.
items.fullText: Acclimatization refers to any of the numerous gradual, long-term responses of an organism to changes in its environment. Such responses are more or less habitual and reversible should environmental conditions revert to an earlier state. The numerous sudden changes that evoke rapid and short-term responses via the nervous and hormonal systems are not examples of acclimatization. An individual organism can regulate its internal processes rapidly to sustain itself within the usual range of environmental changes that it encounters hourly or daily. items.beginnerText: Acclimatization is when an animal or plant slowly gets used to changes in its environment. These changes happen over a long time. The animal or plant can go back to how it was before if the environment changes back. Sudden changes that cause quick reactions are not acclimatization. Animals and plants can quickly control their bodies to live with normal, small changes in the environment. This quick control is called homeostasis. But homeostasis cannot deal with big changes, like summer to winter. As summer ends, animals and plants slowly change for the coming winter. This slow change is acclimatization.
items.intermediateText: Acclimatization is when an organism gradually adapts to changes in its environment over a long period. These adaptations are generally habitual and can be reversed if environmental conditions return to their previous state. However, sudden changes that cause rapid, short-term responses through the nervous and hormonal systems are not considered acclimatization. Organisms can quickly regulate their internal processes to maintain themselves within the typical range of environmental changes they face daily. This rapid regulation, known as homeostasis, has limits. Homeostatic regulation is not effective for large environmental shifts, such as those needed for a plant or animal to adapt from summer's warmth to winter's cold. As summer ends, organisms adjust their behavior and physical state in anticipation of winter. This gradual adjustment to new conditions is acclimatization.

items.title: #807 Reinforcement Theory
items.answerText: In contrast to some other motivational theories, reinforcement theory ignores the inner state of the individual. Instead it focuses on what happens to an individual when he or she __performs/reforms/conforms/confirms__ some task or action. Rather than internal thoughts or desires, the theory is that behaviors are controlled by reinforcers — any consequence that, when immediately following a response, increases the __probability/tendency/potency/capability__ that the behavior will be repeated. For example, you decided to work over the weekend to finish a project early for your boss. When your boss finds out about your extra effort, she thanks you and buys you lunch. Assuming your boss’s reactions were __favorable/comparable/reliable/incomparable__ to you, you will be more likely to do similar deeds in the future. If your boss said or did nothing to acknowledge your extra work, you would be less likely to __demonstrate/galvanize/legislate/commemorate__ similar behavior in the future.

It involves the listener setting aside their own thoughts to concentrate on what the speaker is actually saying, instead of what the listener assumes they are saying. After the scans, the volunteers were asked to __bid/arid/avid/bud__ money in a competitive auction for the food they wanted to have for a snack. Compared to food containing just carbs or fat, the team found that foods high in both of these together __provoked/convoked/evoked/revoked__ far more activity in the brain’s striatum – a region involved in reward that releases the feel-good chemical dopamine. The volunteers were also willing to pay more for the snacks that were high in both carbs and fat, despite all the food items having the same calorific value.

Studies were only in one country or in labs. Or, people wrote about their own sleep, which was not always correct. Kelton Minor at the University of Copenhagen used data to learn more. He looked at sleep trackers worn by 48,000 people in 68 countries from 2015 to 2017. He used this sleep data and weather data. He found that hot nights make people sleep less. Yet an increasing body of research has led doctors to believe that chronic pain should be treated as a disease in its own right, rather than an __enduring/endurance/endurable/endured__ symptom of tissue damage or physical trauma. This could have major __implications/improvisations/importations/supplications__ for the treatment of lasting pain, together with the way we prescribe addictive opioids. Recent research has revealed that in some people, chronic pain is a problem with the brain. An injury can lead to pain that __persists/demands/perceives/tastes__ after the tissue has recovered because the brain has rewired itself and learned to send pain signals, despite there no longer being a reason. Known as central sensitization, it is as if the volume has been turned up on pain.

items.title: #851 Sliced Apples

This __triggers/simplifies/fosters/constricts__ an enzyme known as polyphenol oxidase (PPO) to oxidize polyphenols in the apple’s flesh. This results in new chemicals (o-quinones), which then react with amino acids to produce brown-colored melanins. Different apple varieties contain different amounts of both the initial enzyme and the polyphenols, and thus they brown at different rates. Enzymatic browning is not __unique/contended/related/profiled__ to apples; pears, bananas, and eggplants also turn brown fairly quickly when cut. Enzymatic browning is also responsible for the desirable dark color of prunes, coffee, black tea, and cocoa. Scientists are working to genetically __engineer/designate/envelope/dilute__ apples that do not produce the PPO enzyme, so perhaps brown apples will someday be a thing of the past.

Although chlorophyll itself is harmless, its presence indicates an increased production of solanine, a glycoalkaloid. Solanine protects potatoes and other plants in the Solanaceae family from being eaten by animals. It also helps preserve the sprouting potato. Solanine is a neurotoxin. If humans eat enough of it, it can cause nausea and headaches, and may even lead to serious neurological problems or death. A study suggested that a 16-oz (450-gram) fully green potato could make a small adult sick. Cooking does not destroy solanine, so all green parts of potatoes should be removed. Green potatoes are particularly dangerous for children, as their smaller bodies are more vulnerable to poisoning.

items.fullText: There has been a great variety of critical approach to Shakespeare's work since his death. During the 17th and 18th centuries, Shakespeare was both admired and condemned. Since then, much of the adverse criticism has not been considered relevant, although certain issues have continued to interest critics throughout the years. For instance, charges against his moral propriety were made by Samuel Johnson in the 18th century and by George Bernard Shaw in the 20th. Early criticism was directed primarily at questions of form. Shakespeare was criticized for mixing comedy and tragedy and failing to observe the unities of time and place prescribed by the rules of classical drama. Dryden and Johnson were among the critics claiming that he had corrupted the language with false wit, puns, and ambiguity. Shakespeare was criticized for combining comedy and tragedy and for not following the classical drama rules about time and place. Critics like Dryden and Johnson claimed he damaged the language with poor jokes, puns, and unclear writing. While some early plays may have used these devices too much, 20th-century criticism has generally praised their use in later plays for adding depth and richer meaning.

items.fullText: What killed off the dinosaurs? The end of the Cretaceous Period saw one of the most dramatic mass extinctions the Earth has ever seen. The fossil record shows that throughout their 160-million-year existence , dinosaurs took on a huge variety of forms as the environment changed and new species evolved that were suited to these new conditions. Others that failed to adapt went extinct. But then 66 million years ago, over a relatively short time, dinosaurs disappeared completely (except for birds). Many other animals also died out, including pterosaurs, large marine reptiles, and other sea creatures such as ammonites. Although the number of dinosaur species was already declining, this suggests a sudden catastrophic event sealed their fate, causing unfavorable changes to the environment more quickly than dinosaurs and other creatures could adapt. The exact nature of this catastrophic event is still open to scientific debate. The catastrophe could have been an asteroid impact, volcanic eruptions or the effect of both, together with more gradual changes in the Earth's climate over millions of years. Whatever the causes, the huge extinction that ended the age of the dinosaur left gaps in the ecosystem that were subsequently filled by mammals and birds, allowing them to evolve rapidly.
items.beginnerText: What made the dinosaurs die? The end of the Cretaceous Period had one of the biggest mass extinctions ever on Earth. Fossils show that for 160 million years, dinosaurs changed a lot. New kinds of dinosaurs grew as the world changed. They were right for the new world. The dinosaurs that did not change died. Then, 66 million years ago, the dinosaurs died quickly (except for birds). Many other animals died too. These animals include pterosaurs, big sea reptiles, and sea animals like ammonites. The number of dinosaurs was already going down. But this dying suggests something sudden killed them. The world changed too fast for dinosaurs and other animals to live. Scientists still argue about what this event was. It could have been an asteroid, volcanoes, or both. Earth's climate also changed slowly over millions of years. Whatever the reason, the dinosaurs' extinction made space in the world. Then mammals and birds grew fast.
items.intermediateText: What caused the dinosaurs to die out? The end of the Cretaceous Period was marked by one of the most significant mass extinctions in Earth's history. The fossil record indicates that during their 160-million-year existence, dinosaurs evolved into diverse forms as the environment shifted, and new species adapted to these conditions. Those that could not adapt became extinct. However, 66 million years ago, dinosaurs disappeared relatively quickly (except for birds). Numerous other animals also went extinct, including pterosaurs, large marine reptiles, and sea creatures like ammonites. Even though dinosaur species were already decreasing, this points to a sudden catastrophic event that sealed their fate, causing rapid environmental changes that dinosaurs and other creatures could not adapt to. The specific nature of this catastrophic event is still debated by scientists. The catastrophe could have been caused by an asteroid impact, volcanic eruptions, or a combination of both, along with gradual climate changes over millions of years. Regardless of the causes, the mass extinction that ended the age of the dinosaurs created opportunities in the ecosystem that mammals and birds then filled, allowing them to evolve quickly.
